The earlier version had a bug: `(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])` inserts a space before every capital, so `"a B"` became `"a  B"` with a double space. The version below only inserts a space when a word character comes right before the capital. I ran it on the edge cases (`"Python"`, `"GetCapitalWords"`, `"ABC"`, `"a B"`, `""`, `"helloWorld"`) and all gave the expected output.

```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<=\w)(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```

Of the two options in the team note, the leading-space one fails `capital_words_spaces("Python") == 'Python'`. The `(\w)([A-Z])` variant works for `"GetCapitalWords"` but turns `"ABC"` into `"A BC"`, because the consumed character can't anchor the next match. The lookbehind avoids both problems.

CONFIDENCE: 85
